description: The bar chart illustrates the number of morphosyntactic probing tasks performed on multilingual BERT models, categorized by language family or group, as presented in the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models.” The vertical axis lists ten language categories: IE-Slavic, IE-Romance, IE-Germanic, Uralic, IE-Baltic, IE-other, IE-Indic, Semitic, Turkic, and Basque, arranged from top to bottom in descending order of task count. The horizontal axis, labeled “# tasks,” ranges from 0 to 80 in increments of 10, representing the total number of probing tasks per group. Each category is represented by a distinct colored horizontal bar extending rightward from the y-axis. IE-Slavic has the longest bar, reaching approximately 79 tasks, followed by IE-Romance at ~47, IE-Germanic at ~44, and Uralic at ~20. IE-Baltic and IE-other are near 17 and 15 tasks respectively, while IE-Indic and Semitic are around 10 and 8. Turkic and Basque have the fewest tasks, at approximately 5 and 4 respectively. The bars are not grouped or stacked, and no error bars or annotations are present; the chart uses a simple color-coded scheme to distinguish categories without a legend, relying on visual association. The overall trend shows a steep decline in task coverage from Indo-European subgroups to non-Indo-European families.
